A maximal triangle-free graph is one where adding any missing edge would create a triangle. The complete bipartite graph K_{3,5} with partitions A={0,2,7} and B={1,3,4,5,6} satisfies this: it has no edges within partitions (so no triangles), and every missing edge connects two vertices in the same partition, which would create a triangle with any vertex from the other partition. The fixed edges (0,6) and (2,6) are present as they connect vertices across the partitions. The solution has 15 edges, which is the maximum possible for a triangle-free graph on 8 vertices (Mantel's theorem: floor(8^2/4)=16, but with the fixed edges constraining the partition sizes, 15 is achievable).
